title: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2610.33024v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Harness self-evolution offers a practical route for LLM agents to improve from execution experience without updating model parameters. Its effectiveness depends on whether models can successfully act on the guidance provided by their harnesses. However, we find that harness benefits are not uniform across model capabilities: skills that improve stronger models can provide little benefit or even degrade performance for weaker ones. Across seven models and three benchmarks, we identify 103 task-skill pairs where skills improve GPT-5.6-luna by 31.1 points but degrade Gemma-4-E4B by 8.8 points. In 86% of failed weak-model runs, the violated requirement is already stated in the skill. This motivates skill adaptation: reformulating existing skills to match the executor's capabilities and make their guidance easier to execute. To achieve this, we diagnose failures in tool execution, context management, instruction following, and verification,

translated_title: 演化以匹配能力：通过技能适应改进框架自我演化
translated_abstract: 框架自我演化为大语言模型智能体提供了一条从执行经验中改进的实用途径，且无需更新模型参数。其有效性取决于模型能否成功执行其框架所提供的指导。然而，我们发现框架带来的收益在不同模型能力之间并不一致：能够提升强模型表现的技能，对弱模型可能收效甚微甚至造成性能下降。在七个模型和三个基准测试中，我们识别出103个任务-技能对，其中技能使GPT-5.6-luna提升了31.1分，却使Gemma-4-E4B下降了8.8分。在86%的弱模型失败运行中，被违反的要求其实已在技能中明确说明。这启发了技能适应这一方法：重新表述现有技能，使其与执行者的能力相匹配，并使其指导更易于执行。为实现这一目标，我们对工具执行、上下文管理、指令遵循和验证等环节的失败进行诊断，
tldr: 该论文发现框架技能对不同能力的大模型收益不均，提出“技能适应”方法，通过诊断工具执行、上下文管理、指令遵循和验证等环节的失败，重新表述现有技能以匹配执行者能力，从而改进LLM智能体的框架自我演化效果。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that harness-provided skills benefit models unevenly across capability levels, and proposes "skill adaptation"—diagnosing failures in tool execution, context management, instruction following, and verification, then reformulating existing skills to match the executor's capabilities—to improve harness self-evolution of LLM agents.
